Base-Catalyzed Sequential 1,4-Addition/Intramolecular Cyclization/
Aromatization Reaction: Synthesis of Benzofuro[3,2 ‑b]pyridines
Yimin Hu, Wangyu Shi, Zhengyang Yan, Jianning Liao, Min Liu, Jiaqing Xu, Wei Wang, Yongjun Wu,
Cheng Zhang, * and Hongchao Guo *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 6780 −6783 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: An e ﬃcient K 2CO3-catalyzed 1,4-addition/intra-
molecular cyclization/aromatization reaction of aurone-derived 1-
azadienes with trisubstituted allenoates has been developed, giving
a series of benzofuro[3,2- b]pyridines in moderate to excellent
yields. The reaction proceeded e ﬃciently under an air atmosphere
without the use of transition metal catalysts. This protocol provides
a concise approach to benzofuro[3,2- b]pyridines.
P
olyheterocyclic frameworks are ubiquitous in natural
products and pharmacologically active molecules. 1
Among them, benzofuro[3,2- b]pyridines (BFPs) ( Figure 1 )
represent an important class of heterocyclic compounds. 2−5
Various strategies for their construction have been estab-
lished.6−9 However, some of these methods su ﬀer from
multistep procedures and the limitation of a narrow substrate
range. Therefore, it still is highly desirable to develop a simple
method for the construction of this important sca ﬀold.
In recent years, aurone-derived 1-azadienes have been used
as highly reactive intermediates in organic synthesis, due to the
driving force of aromatization.
7−10 With these aurone-derived
1-azadienes as the starting material, several elegant methods for
the construction of benzofuro[3,2- b]pyridine were established.
In 2019, Chen, Jiang and co-workers developed an intriguing
base-promoted [4+1+1] annulation reaction of aurone-derived
1-azadienes with α-bromo carbonyls, providing a complex
benzofuro[3,2-b]pyridines sca ﬀold in an e ﬃcient manner
(Scheme 1 a).
7 By using a copper catalyst, Zhou achieved
formal [4+2] cycloaddition of aurone-derived 1-azadienes with
terminal alkynes, which elegantly produced 1,2-
dihydrobenzofuran[3,2-b]pyridines through a complex nucle-
ophilic addition/cyclization/isomerization process ( Scheme
1b).
8 In 2021, Jiang, Tu, Hao, and co-workers presented a
Lewis acid-catalyzed [2+2] cycloaddition/retroelectrocycliza-
tion/1,6-addition relay of aurone-derived 1-azadienes and 1-
alkynylnaphthalen-2-ols, resulting in the regio- and diaster-
eoselective synthesis of 1,2-dihydrobenzofuro[3,2- b]pyridine
with a chiral carbon center and an axial chirality in good yields
(Scheme 1 c).
9 According to previous studies, 11 it was known
that the α-hydrogen of allenoates and allene ketones has a
certain acidity, which allows allenoates and allene ketones to be
deprotonated and thus act as nucleophiles. On the basis of this

feature, we investigated the base-assisted reaction of allenoates
with aurone-derived 1-azadienes, and we herein describe an
eﬃcient K
2CO3-catalyzed 1,4-addition/intramolecular cycliza-
tion/aromatization reaction of aurone-derived 1-azadienes with
trisubstituted allenoates, giving a series of benzofuro[3,2-
b]pyridines ( Scheme 1 d).
At the beginning of our study, we optimized the reaction of
1-azadiene 1a and trisubstituted allenoate 2a in CH
2Cl2 under
an argon atmosphere. As shown in Table 1, several LB catalysts
were screened (entries 1 −4), but only 4-(dimethylamino)-
pyridine (DMAP) led to the corresponding product 3a in 23%
yield (entry 4). Subsequently, we turned our attention to
inorganic bases. To our delight, in the presence of 20 mol %
K
2CO3, product 3a was obtained in 81% yield (entry 5).
Na2CO3 did not catalyze this reaction (entry 6). With Cs 2CO3
as the catalyst, product 3a was obtained in 52% yield (entry 7).
With the use of K 2CO3 as the catalyst, several solvents were
then screened (entries 8 −11), indicating that tetrahydrofuran
was the optimal solvent for this reaction (entry 8). The
structure of product 3a has been unambiguously con ﬁrmed by
X-ray di ﬀraction analysis.
We accidentally found that when the model reaction mixture
was placed in air, product 3a was obtained in 32% yield after 3
days, and the corresponding aromatization product 4a was also
isolated in 60% yield ( Scheme 2 ). This triggered our
exploration of a one-pot strategy for the synthesis of
aromatized product 4a (Scheme 2 ). After a concise screening,
we found that 1,2-dichloro-4,5-dicyanobenzoquinone (DDQ)
was productive for this aromatization. After the 1,4-addition/
intramolecular cyclization process had reached completion, 1.5
equiv of DDQ was added and product 4a was produced in 87%
yield in one pot.
To study the scope of this process, we investigated the
reaction of various 1-azadienes 1 and di ﬀerent trisubstituted
allenoates 2, as shown in Table 2 . The results indicated that
the position, steric properties, and electronic properties of the
substituents on the aromatic ring of 1-azadienes 1 and the
benzene ring of allenoates 2 had little e ﬀect on the reactivities.
When the R
1 group was an alkyl group, the high reactivity was
maintained, and product 4af was formed in 80% yield. The
impact of the R 2 group of the allenoates 2 linked to the ketone
carbonyl on the reaction was also explored. To our delight,

addition, moderate to good results were gained with 1-
azadienes 1 bearing electron-donating and -withdrawing
groups at the benzofuran moiety (products 4o−4q).
Unfortunately, when the Ar group in 1-azadiene 1 was tert-
butyl, the reaction did not work.
As indicated in Scheme 3, when this reaction was performed
with 2 mmol (750 mg) of aurone-derived 1-azadiene 1a, the
reaction still worked well to produce product 4a in 86% yield.
There was an only slight loss of yield, compared with the
reaction at a 0.1 mmol scale. Reduction of product 4a with
sodium borohydride gave glycol product 5 in 56% yield with
>20:1 dr.
The proposed reaction mechanism for the reaction is shown
in Scheme 4 . Initially, trisubstituted allenoate 2a is
deprotonated in the presence of K
2CO3 to provide allene
carbanion Int-1. Subsequent 1,4-addition of intermediate Int-1
to 1-azadiene 1a led to the formation of tetrasubstituted
allenoate intermediate Int-2. Intramolecular cyclization of Int-
2 produced intermediate Int-3, which underwent a proton
transfer to give 1,4-dihydrobenzofuro[3,2- b]pyridine 3a. The
succeeding aromatization occurred in the presence of DDQ to
provide the ﬁnal product, benzofuro[3,2- b]pyridine 4a.
In summary, we have disclosed a concise one-pot synthesis
of benzofuro[3,2- b]pyridines through an e ﬃcient K 2CO3-
catalyzed 1,4-addition/intramolecular cyclization/aromatiza-
tion sequence. A series of benzofuro[3,2- b]pyridines were
obtained in moderate to excellent yields. This approach
features cheap K
2CO3 as a catalyst, mild reaction conditions,
and a wide range of substrates.
